assertions: Output does not delete the order based solely on req.params.id with authentication as the only check
Output adds an explicit check that the order belongs to req.user (e.g. querying/deleting scoped by both _id and the authenticated user's id) before deleting it
Output returns a 403 or 404 when the order doesn't belong to the authenticated user, rather than deleting it or a generic success
Output does not scope the query by invoice id alone
Output scopes the query (or an ORM/row-level-security equivalent) by both the invoice id and the authenticated user's id
Output returns a 403/404 rather than another user's invoice data when the id belongs to a different user
Output does not use req.body.userId to determine which user's profile is updated
Output derives the acting user's id from the authenticated session/token (e.g. req.user.id) instead of a client-supplied field
Output does not simply validate that req.body.userId matches req.user.id as the primary fix without also removing the client's ability to specify the acting identity
Output does not return messages for an arbitrary :id with authentication as the only check
Output adds an explicit authorization check confirming req.params.id matches the authenticated user (or an otherwise-granted relationship) before returning the messages
Output treats this read endpoint with the same rigor as a state-changing endpoint rather than assuming reads are lower-risk
